items.markingKey: (d) Correct: "A body that is a good absorber of radiation is also a good emitter." The other three are false.
options: A good absorber of radiation is a poor emitter.
Heat from the Sun reaches the Earth by convection.
Conduction requires bulk motion of matter.
A body that is a good absorber of radiation is also a good emitter.

items.stem:
Aditya's family uses a 1000 W electric kettle to boil 2 kg of water starting at 20 °C. (c = 4186 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, L_v = 2.256 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹; assume no losses)
(i) How much heat brings the water to 100 °C? (ii) How long does this take? (iii) How much longer to boil away 0.1 kg of it? (iv) Why does the temperature stay at 100 °C while it boils?
items.answer: (i) 6.70 × 10⁵ J (ii) 670 s (iii) 226 s (iv) heat goes into latent heat of vaporisation
items.markingKey: (i) mcΔT (1). (ii) Q/P (1). (iii) mL/P (1). (iv) latent heat, no temperature change (1).

items.stem: How much heat is needed to convert 20 g of ice at −20 °C completely into steam at 100 °C? (c_ice = 2100 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, c_water = 4186 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, L_f = 3.34 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹, L_v = 2.256 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹)
items.markingKey: Q₁ = m c_ice × 20 = 840 J; Q₂ = mL_f = 6680 J; Q₃ = m c_w × 100 = 8372 J; Q₄ = mL_v = 45120 J (1 each + 1 for total) = 61000 J.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about Newton's law of cooling is correct?
items.answer: A hot body cools faster at first and slower later.
items.markingKey: (b) Correct: "A hot body cools faster at first and slower later." The other three are false.
options: A body cools slower when its temperature is higher.
A hot body cools faster at first and slower later.
A hot body cools at a constant rate until it reaches room temperature.
The cooling curve is a straight line.

items.stem: A steel rail is 10 m long at 10 °C. By how much does its length increase when it is heated to 30 °C? (α_steel = 1.2 × 10⁻⁵ K⁻¹)
How much heat is needed to raise the temperature of 0.5 kg of iron by 40 °C? (Specific heat capacity of iron = 450 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹)
A blackbody at 127 °C is heated until its absolute temperature becomes 2 times. By what factor does the power it radiates increase?
items.markingKey: P ∝ T⁴ (Stefan-Boltzmann) ⇒ factor = 2⁴ = 16.0. (Note: use kelvin, 400 K → 800 K.)

items.stem: Which term is described by: transfer of heat by electromagnetic waves, needing no medium?
items.markingKey: (a) radiation: transfer of heat by electromagnetic waves, needing no medium.
options: radiation
convection

conduction

items.stem: A steel rail of cross-sectional area 50 cm² is fixed rigidly at both ends so that it cannot expand. If its temperature rises by 10 °C, find the thermal stress and the force on the supports. (α = 1.2 × 10⁻⁵ K⁻¹, Y = 2.0 × 10¹¹ N m⁻²)
items.markingKey: Prevented strain = αΔT = 1.20 × 10⁻⁴ (1); stress = Y αΔT = 2.40 × 10⁷ N m⁻² (1); F = stress × A = 1.20 × 10⁵ N (1).
